clue.text: American money going to drug-taking terrorists to get a simple meal

parts.note: jack is US slang for money

indicators.note: the terrorists are taking something in, so the drug goes inside their name

explanation.surface: Dollars flow to a gang of drug-using terrorists, who then grab a quick bite.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA was the Basque separatist group; jack is American slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked potato served in its skin is a plain, cheap lunch or supper dish.

clue.text: Alias (right?) in ( yes!) German capital

indicators.note: the alias and the right are placed in the middle of the German word

explanation.surface: A puzzled aside about an alias, with an exclamatory German yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The German word for yes splits around the alias and the right; 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jakarta is the capital city of Indonesia, on the island of Java.

clue.text: Work history includes working with one before court and one inside

indicators.note: the work record includes something, holding it within its letters

parts.note: curriculum vitae, a record of someone's employment
as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A job history that records employment before a court case and a spell inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'one inside' is the definition, slang for someone in prison; the earlier 'one' is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside is slang for being in prison, and a person serving a sentence there is a convict.

clue.text: Get rid of emigr* carrying timber (dishonoured) to Spain

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispose of a disgraced emigre hauling wood to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The honour removed is the MBE, a British order; the emigre's last letter is garbled in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to root out or destroy completely, an emphatic way of removing.

clue.text: Assume there's one in the mail

indicators.note: something sits in the mail, so it goes within the word for mail

explanation.surface: A guess that a letter is waiting in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a premise, taking something as given for argument.

clue.text: Commotion curtailed on American burial place

indicators.note: curtailed literally means its tail is cut off, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A disturbance cut short at an American cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumulus is an ancient mound of earth raised over a grave, a prehistoric barrow.

clue.text: Line about stray dog

indicators.note: the line goes about, around, the other word

parts.note: to wander from the right path

explanation.surface: A queue forming around a stray dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Terriers are a group of small energetic breeds bred for hunting vermin, so one kind of dog.

clue.text: Orchestra and opera house introduce cosy arrangement for infrequent visitor

indicators.note: the orchestra and opera house introduce, bring between them, the rearranged letters
an arrangement of the word puts its letters in a new order

parts.note: the Metropolitan Opera in New York

explanation.surface: A musical event where orchestra and opera house put on something intimate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Halle is Manchester's orchestra, the Met New York's opera house; scrambled COSY goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Halley's Comet returns to the inner solar system only about every 76 years, a rare caller.

clue.text: Plant stalk an etching features

indicators.note: the phrase features the solution within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A botanical print of a plant whose stem appears in an etching.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkanet is a plant of the borage family, whose root yields a red dye.

clue.text: Swordsman's one lily-like reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the string of pieces is read backwards

explanation.surface: A swordsman pondering a lily, or a flower that seems to reflect him.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; I, ARUM and AS are joined then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan, famous for their swords.

clue.text: Planting seeds in half the country

explanation.surface: Sowing seed across half of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests farming, but the seeds are reproductive ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Insemination is introducing semen to fertilise, figuratively a sowing of seed.

clue.text: Story about boat ride's beginning to get more mischievous

the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A tale about a boat trip that turns more playful.
explanation.walkthrough: The ride's letter is added after the story has wrapped the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Larky means given to pranks and fun, so larkier is more playful or roguish.

clue.text: Stories about "The King and I" and suchlike productions

definitions.text: "The King and I" and suchlike productions

indicators.note: the stories go about, around, the other letters

explanation.surface: Tales about a famous musical film and others like it.
explanation.walkthrough: The King and I is a 1956 film musical, so the title doubles as wordplay and as an example within the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Talkies is the old term for films with soundtracks, such as that musical film.

clue.text: Point to unknown source of ferment

explanation.surface: Indicating a mysterious cause of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The point is joined on to the unknown, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that causes fermentation in brewing and baking.

clue.text: Toper's first into liquor-producing plant — liquor's an immuniser

indicators.note: one letter is put into the name of the plant

indicators.note: the drinker's first means only the opening letter of that word

explanation.surface: A drunkard sampling spirits in a distillery, and the liquor as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: A toper is a heavy drinker; the 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiserum is blood serum carrying antibodies, given to confer immunity against a disease.

clue.text: Long shot at pachyderm dropping insect in toto

indicators.note: what remains is placed in the phrase that follows
the beast drops, sheds, the small creature from its letters

explanation.surface: A wildlife photographer's distant shot of an elephant, which ends up squashing a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: In toto is Latin for 'entirely', but here the second word is just letters to hold the trimmed beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens magnifies distant subjects, so a telephoto is a picture taken from far off.

clue.text: Watch and leer over gymnastic performance

indicators.note: knocked over, the letters tumble into a different order

explanation.surface: A spectator ogling an athlete's routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is a sideways handspring with arms and legs extended like spokes, a basic gymnastic move.

clue.text: Swilling a Strine wine?

indicators.note: swilling sloshes things around, mixing up the letters

parts.note: Strine is jocular for Australian English

explanation.surface: An Australian knocking back a glass of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Strine is a humorous name for broad Australian speech; the question mark flags that the Aussie would hardly drink a Greek wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white or rosé wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: The wild wendigo bird

indicators.note: running wild, the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: a cannibal spirit of Algonquian legend

explanation.surface: A monster of North American folklore pictured as a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The widgeon, also spelled wigeon, is a dabbling duck with a whistling call.

clue.text: The writer's a mug

definitions.meaning: Gertrude, the American author of The Making of Americans

explanation.surface: An insult: the author is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug looks like British slang for a dupe, but it is a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was a modernist author; a stein is also a large earthenware beer tankard.

clue.text: Standing parliaments entertaining alternative drug

explanation.walkthrough: DIETS reversed gives STEID, which takes OR in.
explanation.definitionFit: Steroids are a class of compounds used as medicines and, notoriously, as performance-enhancing drugs.

clue.text: Inspire fondness and mounting regret about the state

the regret goes about, around, the state

explanation.surface: Falling in love while sorrow about the nation grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The state' is a specific country, the Gulf sultanate, not a general word for nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to fill them with love or delight, captivating them.

clue.text: A little bit more (but not all) about the killer

explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter whose role is to kill the bull at the climax.

clue.text: "Fiddler's gum" is counted among the maestro's infirmities

indicators.note: the solution is counted among, sits within, the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A conductor's ailments include a sticky musical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin violinists rub on bows for grip, a gum used by fiddlers.

clue.text: Carpets arranged in blocks

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh into another order

explanation.surface: Rugs laid out in squares, like carpet tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: precast concrete is made in blocks before being put in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Precast describes concrete moulded into units off-site, so it comes ready-made as sections.

clue.text: Last words on instant muscle

explanation.surface: Final remarks on a moment, then a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: Individual backing secures gold ring for sherry

parts.note: a solo is a performance by one

explanation.walkthrough: Or is gold in heraldry; the reversal covers the solo and gold together, and the ring is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich, nutty style of sherry from Jerez.

clue.text: May no neo-Nazis get more rum for hapless other ranks?

parts.note: the National Front, a British far-right party

explanation.surface: A wish that far-right extremists won't be given more drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Front is a British far-right party; rum is British for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannon fodder means soldiers treated as expendable, the ordinary ranks sent to die.
